observations: A large circular black outline dominates the center, enclosing layered warm tones—deep red, burnt orange, and olive—with white zigzag marks and black spiked forms in the lower half suggesting a jaw with visible tooth-like white verticals.
Loose scribbled lines in red, light blue, white, and pink radiate outward from the central form against a flat teal-green ground, with a horizontal pink band cutting across the left edge.
On the right side, a tighter cluster of yellow, gold, and black lines forms a secondary rounded shape containing a small spiral, distinct from the looser marks surrounding it.
reading: A heavy circular outline holds a dense interior of warm reds and oranges, while spiked black forms and white zigzag verticals below read as a jaw with bared teeth. The surrounding field is restless—thin colored lines scatter outward without settling. The right-side spiral cluster sits quieter against the louder central mass. Whether the overall effect feels confrontational or absorbing is left to the viewer.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between nnotb #206 and nnotb #208 in both title and recorded creation order. All three share a teal-green ground and a large circular form with jaw-like marks, but #207 carries warmer interior tones than either neighbor.

connections.reason: nnotb #208 shares the same teal ground and large circular skull-like form, but its interior is darker and more densely overworked, making the two a direct contrast in interior density on the same basic structure.
nnotb #206 uses a cooler blue-grey ground and a horizontally oriented jaw form, contrasting with #207's warmer interior palette and more upright circular framing.

lookingQuestion: What does the relationship between the tight spiral cluster on the right and the tooth-like verticals at the center do to how you move through the image?
ambiguities: The secondary rounded form on the right could be read as a separate figure or as a detail of the same form; the image does not resolve this.
